# Getting Started {#sec-usage}

## Installation

The solver and the viewer are two Python packages (Python ≥ 3.12) from one
repository. On a cluster, install only the solver:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/IMTEK-Simulation/DropletRelaxer.git
cd DropletRelaxer
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .               # DropletRelaxer: numpy, scipy, h5py
pip install -e viewer          # DropletViewer: + pyvista, vtk, imageio (for a desktop)
```

## Running a scenario

A scenario is a TOML file that sets only what differs from the defaults
(@sec-usage-configuration). The repository has a few in `examples/`.

```bash
droplet-relax run examples/sessile.toml -o sessile.vtkhdf  # headless, writes the run file
droplet-relax info sessile.vtkhdf                          # summary
droplet-view sessile.vtkhdf                                # window: replay with history slider
droplet-view sessile.vtkhdf --video sessile.mp4            # the replay as a video, no window
droplet-view live examples/default.toml                    # solver + live window in one process
```

`droplet-view live` writes the run to `runs/<timestamp>/run.vtkhdf` (or `-o`)
while showing it; after the run the window replays that file. The Stop button
or closing the window ends the run cleanly. `droplet-view run.vtkhdf --follow`
watches a run file that another process (e.g. a cluster job on a shared file
system) is still writing.

Any parameter can be overridden on the command line, in TOML syntax:

```bash
droplet-relax run examples/default.toml -o theta120.vtkhdf --set solver.contact_angle_deg=120 \
    --set obstacle.center_end=[30,0,125]
droplet-relax show-config examples/default.toml     # the complete effective configuration, documented
```

## Cluster runs and restarts

`droplet-relax` needs no display and no VTK. Parameter sweeps are job arrays
that differ only in `--set` options; `examples/slurm_contact_angle_sweep.sh`
is a template. SLURM sends SIGTERM before the wall-time limit
(`--signal=TERM@300`); `droplet-relax` then finishes the current iteration,
writes the final frame and a checkpoint, and exits. Checkpoints are also
written every `output.checkpoint_every` iterations, so a killed run loses at
most that many. Continue with

```bash
droplet-relax restart run.vtkhdf [--set solver.n_iterations=2000000]
```

A restart continues bit-identically to an uninterrupted run. Only
`solver.n_iterations` and `output.*` can change at a restart; anything else is
a new run.

## Tests

```bash
pip install -e ".[test]" -e "viewer[test]"
pytest                    # fast tests (seconds)
pytest -m slow            # real relaxations, reference runs (minutes)
pytest -m ""              # everything
pytest test/test_force.py::test_force_equals_minus_energy_derivative   # a single slow test, by node id
```
